solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Got into bed with a criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the preceding words are bent out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scandalous tale of someone who slept with a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got into bed with' reads as one phrase, but 'Got' alone is the definition and 'with' only joins it to the letters that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To have obtained something is simply to have acquired or got hold of it.

clue.text: Crowd turning on poet in blitz

indicators.note: turning round makes the word face the other way, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a mob is an unruly crowd
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A mob rounds on a poet during the wartime bombing of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' here only means 'placed next to', joining the two pieces; 'blitz' is used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To blitz a place is to attack it intensively, especially with sustained shelling or bombs.

clue.text: Cartel audit going wrong, it's said

indicators.note: when things go wrong they fall into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rumour has it an audit of a cartel has gone awry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' looks like a homophone signal, but 'said' is the definition and 'it's' just links it.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that are articulated are spoken or expressed clearly, so the term works as a synonym for uttered.

clue.text: Indian leader employing some dour henchmen from the south

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the south means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
the phrase uses only part of what follows, so the answer sits inside the clue's words

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of dour and the start of henchmen

explanation.surface: A political boss in India hires grim-faced heavies from the south of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of independent India, a national leader.

clue.text: Collapse of penthouse maybe owned by banker

indicators.note: what is owned is held by its owner, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river, and a banker is crosswordese for a river (it has banks)
a penthouse is an example of a flat; 'maybe' signals the example

explanation.surface: Talk of a slump in the value of a luxury top-floor apartment belonging to a financier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' suggests a financier, but it is a river: something that has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflate is to let the air out, so the thing collapses or goes flat.

clue.text: Reveal all after country club investigation quietly dropped

parts.note: the United Nations is, playfully, a club whose members are countries

indicators.note: something dropped is let go and left out, so that letter disappears from the word

parts.note: a probe is an investigation
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A golf-club scandal is hushed up, and only then does someone tell all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country club' looks like a golf club but is a witty description of the UN. 'Reveal all' is taken literally: to take off all one's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrobe is to undress, so one literally reveals everything.

clue.text: Poet hurls out pad

indicators.note: the letters are thrown out of their places and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A furious poet throws a writing pad away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pad' looks like a notepad being hurled, but it is a verb: to stuff with padding.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster furniture is to fit it with padding, springs and covering, that is, to pad it.

clue.text: Warning sign the Speaker's studied

indicators.note: what a speaker says reaches us by ear, so we go by the sound of the next word

parts.note: read, past tense of read, means studied and is pronounced like the colour

explanation.surface: A warning notice that the parliamentary Speaker has looked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Speaker' suggests the Speaker of the House of Commons, but it only signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is the colour of danger, used on stop lights and warning notices.

clue.text: Young criminal describing time of his life?

parts.note: a boy is a young male
a hood is a gangster, short for hoodlum

explanation.surface: A young delinquent recounts what he got up to as a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'time of his life' is not a happy time but a stage of a male life.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyhood is the period of a man's life when he is a boy, hence a time of his life.

clue.text: Best wedding programme?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: a match is a marriage
second meaning: the BBC's long-running football highlights show

explanation.walkthrough: Match means a marriage as well as a game; the answer is the BBC's long-running Saturday-night football highlights show.
explanation.definitionFit: The best marriage of the day would be its finest match, and the phrase is the title of a British TV football programme.

clue.text: Eastern people's side welcoming different temperatures

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Man U, short for Manchester United, a football side
C and H for cold and hot, the two different temperatures on taps

explanation.surface: An oriental nation's team takes on varied climates.
explanation.walkthrough: Manchester United is an English football club, commonly called Man U.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manchu are a people of north-east China, who founded the Qing dynasty.

clue.text: Mention a misapprehension that head has left

indicators.note: once the head is gone, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
an illusion is a false belief

explanation.surface: Bringing up a misunderstanding that the headteacher has walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: An allusion is an indirect reference, a passing mention of something.

clue.text: Unplanned broadcast of Peanuts soon?

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A surprise screening of the Peanuts cartoon is coming shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: Peanuts is the Charlie Brown comic strip, but here it is just a set of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spontaneous happens on impulse without any prior planning.

clue.text: Teenager thrilled, I hear, by beer drinking party

indicators.note: a drinker takes something in, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a do is a party

indicators.note: what is heard rather than read is taken by its sound alone

parts.note: to be sent is slang for being thrilled or carried away

explanation.surface: Someone excited by beer at a drinks party, a typical youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' means placed beside: the sound-alike sits next to the beer that has the party inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a young person in the years between childhood and adulthood, roughly a teenager.

clue.text: University's new stewards becoming sloppy

indicators.note: sloppy work is disordered, so the letters lose their neat order and rearrange

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: The college's newly hired stewards are getting slapdash.
explanation.definitionFit: St Andrews in Fife is Scotland's oldest university, founded in the fifteenth century.

clue.text: Contents of paper binder, quaintly dated?

indicators.note: the contents are what lies inside, so only the inner part of the word is kept

parts.note: a folder holds loose papers together

explanation.surface: Wondering whether what is in a ring binder of papers is old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: olde is the mock-archaic spelling used to make things sound quaint, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe.
explanation.definitionFit: Olde is a pseudo-antique spelling of old used for quaint effect, so it is old in a twee manner.

clue.text: In recession corporations producing coarse material

indicators.note: a recession is a moving back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a corporation is a jocular British word for a pot belly, so corporations are tums

explanation.surface: Companies hit by an economic downturn put out shoddy goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporations' suggests businesses and 'recession' the economy, but corporation is an old British joke word for a large paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is indecent or obscene material, coarse in the sense of vulgar.

clue.text: Cocktail dress inspiring painting?

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so one piece is drawn inside the other

parts.note: a mini is a short dress
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: Asking whether an evening frock gave an artist ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocktail dress' reads as one item of clothing, but 'Cocktail' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a classic cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: EastEnders failing to provide any hope?

parts.words: EastEnders failing to provide any hope?
parts.note: surface reading: the TV soap set in London's East End offers its viewers no optimism
setter's reading: Cockneys famously drop their aitches, so they fail to give the breathy sound at the start of words

explanation.walkthrough: In phonetics the word names the breathed h sound, which Cockney speakers (East Londoners, as in the BBC soap EastEnders) tend to leave out.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the phonetic sense, the word means an ambition or hope for the future.

clue.text: One fussing a lot about new necklace

indicators.note: to be about something is to go around it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a pedant fusses over small details
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A fusspot frets over a recently bought necklace.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant is a necklace with an ornament hanging from it, or the hanging ornament itself.

clue.text: "Paw" included in dictionary — or not?

indicators.note: what is included goes inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the Oxford English Dictionary
mitt is slang for a hand or paw

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the word paw made it into the dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: 'included … or not' means the opposite of included, that is, left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitted means left out, the reverse of included.

clue.text: After deal crime boss is exploited

indicators.note: the word places one piece following another, setting the order in which they are joined

parts.note: to trade is to deal
a Mafia don is a crime boss

explanation.surface: After striking a bargain, the gangland chief is taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade on something is to take unfair advantage of it, that is, to exploit it.

clue.text: Bitter substance girl preserved apparently

indicators.note: food preserved in a can is sealed inside it, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: one way to preserve food is to tin it
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman kept in good condition turns out to be bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Tannin read as tinned Ann: the girl sits inside the can, and 'apparently' admits the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Tannin is the astringent, bitter compound found in tea, wine and tree bark.

clue.text: Hook up in Asian hotel, did you say?

indicators.note: the question asks what was spoken, so we go by the sound of the words

parts.note: a hotel from Thailand would be a Thai inn

explanation.surface: Arranging to meet up at a hotel somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hook up' suggests a romantic meeting, but it means connect.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a link or connection, as when one product is hooked up with another.

clue.text: Facing equivalent challenges, as punter and companion may be

definitions.meaning: first meaning: idiom for sharing the same difficult situation

definitions.text: as punter and companion may be
definitions.meaning: second meaning, taken literally: a punter propels a flat river boat with a pole, and a passenger rides in it too

explanation.walkthrough: A punter is usually a gambler or customer, but here it is someone punting on a river such as the Cam.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes people sharing the same predicament, and literally two people aboard one vessel.

clue.text: Occasionally stroke a little piggy?

indicators.note: something done only now and then skips in between, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Now and then giving a small pig a pat.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy went to market', each piggy is a child's toe.
explanation.definitionFit: Toes are counted off as little piggies in the familiar children's nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Various people going under

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an archaic adjective for several or sundry
second meaning: those who swim underwater

explanation.walkthrough: 'Going under' suggests failure or sinking, but it just means submerging.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers is an old word for sundry, and also the plural of someone who swims beneath the surface.

clue.text: Journalist I dispatched back to cover unknown English region

indicators.note: sent back means going the other way, so the letters run in reverse
a cover goes over and around something, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: ed is short for editor
taken as written
to dispatch is to send
y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A reporter is posted back north to report on an obscure part of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area of north-east England around Newcastle upon Tyne.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyneside is the conurbation along the River Tyne, a region of England.
